# Portal runtime candidate: internal package 4.3.39

Functional source checkpoint: `069b43b62b3fb589673c4d31f0b4dface6a514a4`.
Prepared on 2026-10-28 for the Portal integrations draft. The compatibility
entry names that separately committed functional source. No bundle digest or
installed result is invented in this preparation record. The legacy package/directory identifier remains
`pixel`; Portal is the public ODS experience. This is an ODS-maintained internal
candidate, not an upstream release or completed platform qualification.

An authorized installed request asked for at most one email. The model instead
called the Inbox read tool with `{ "max": 1 }`, although its actual parameter is
`maxResults`. Deferred dispatch reached the handler without rejecting the
unknown key, and the handler treated `maxResults` as omitted, selecting its
existing default of 50. The result was a schema-admission defect; a prompt that
asks for one email is not an access-control boundary. The count-scope metadata
from 4.3.38 does not enforce the number of records requested by a malformed
argument object.

The Source plugin now uses the release's actual locked TypeBox validator to
check every registered read/proposal tool argument object before reading a
projection or creating a proposal. Top-level argument objects and nested recipient
and attendee objects reject unknown properties. Missing required parameters,
wrong types, invalid bounds and undeclared keys return a fixed repair
instruction containing the declared schema, without copying rejected values.
The Source handler does not clean, coerce, rename or silently retry arguments.
The native dispatcher can perform its own legitimate normalization; this
evidence does not claim to exclude every normalization inside the SDK.
`{ "max": 1 }` reaches Source intact and is rejected instead of widening into
an omitted `maxResults` default.

An empty object remains valid for tools whose schema permits omitted arguments,
and their documented defaults remain unchanged. A valid
`{ "maxResults": 1 }` continues to request one record. This change does not turn
natural-language limits into an ACL, add a per-chat privacy ceiling, change
Source synchronization, expand provider access, or create a new approval or
OAuth system. Existing Google consent, proposals and explicit owner approvals
remain separate boundaries.

Twenty-three Source plugin/dispatch tests and two existing OAuth plugin
controls passed with the real locked TypeBox 1.3.13 builder and validator. The
Source lane includes the real pinned SDK 2026.6.33 Tool Search dispatcher,
without skipping that case. Seven query tests and three release-packaging
controls also passed. Five new regressions were confirmed to fail against the
preceding Source index. Plugin registration, Source projections and surrounding
services remain controlled fixtures. This is not native gateway execution or
evidence that a model will reliably choose or repair the correct arguments.

At this preparation point the 4.3.39 bundle has not been generated, ordinary
installed upgrade and real-model behavior have not been qualified, and no real
account or provider was contacted by this code/metadata work.

The official release-file generator and its consistency check passed for
4.3.39. Current status, platform-reference and document-inventory generators
also passed their independent checks. Four migration-schema cases and three
isolated migration/restore shell fixtures passed with the current 4.3.39
target. These are version-bound fixture checks, not an ordinary installed
upgrade. A comparison to the preceding metadata confirmed dependency/npm
integrities, image/runtime pins, trust policy and all earlier compatibility
rows were preserved.

The version increases from 4.3.38 because a changed held source requires a
strictly increasing package version. OpenClaw, dependencies, image pins and
trust anchors are unchanged. Historical qualification records and supported
bridge-version entries retain their original identifiers. No release signature
is generated or claimed.

The full upstream public-release contract still lacks the historical
`LIVE-AUDIT-4.0.0.md` and `LIVE-AUDIT-4.1.0.md` documents deliberately omitted
from this export. They were not copied or fabricated. Public release acceptance,
native macOS and other required platform/fleet lanes remain open; internal
metadata consistency is not completion of those gates. The full documentation
generator also stops at the omitted historical `LIVE-AUDIT-4.3.27.md`; the
release-evidence index was not regenerated by fabricating that document or
waiving its evidence requirement.
